Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board (Board) on any

card to the Secretary. The Board will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The
Board will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Board may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Board
meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Board:
  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the Board as a whole and not directed to individual Board members.

available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when
services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Board regarding any item on this agenda after it has been posted will also be

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the Community Development Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during

Chair Apodaca called the special hybrid meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Norwalk City
Hall, Council Chambers and via video/teleconference pursuant to the provisions of
Assembly Bill 361. Responding to roll call were Board Member Barragan and Chair
Apodaca in person, and Board Members Garcia, Navas, and Vice Chair Lopez via
videoconference. Also present were John P. Ramirez, Director of Community
Development, Maged Soliman, Building and Safety Manager, Ozzie Ramos, Director of
Public Safety; Gabriela Garcia, Management Analyst; Jaime Cortez, Code Compliance
Inspector; Andrew Arellano, Assistant Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative
Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES
The Board approved the minutes of the Regular Meeting of June 22, 2022.

REPORT OF DELINQUENT TRASH ACCOUNTS

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Gabriela Garcia, Senior
Management Analyst, presented a report stating that the City of Norwalk provides
mandatory refuse service to protect the public health and welfare of its residents; that, as
such, Athens Services picks up trash weekly billing customers on a quarterly basis; that
payment for services is due within thirty (30) days from the billing date; that a late fee of
$25.00 is added if payment has not been made by the end of the service quarter; that the
hauler makes attempts during the year to collect on past-due accounts; that as authorized
in the Municipal Code, the hauler is allowed to seek payment through the tax rolls in
August of each year for the period of May 1st of the previous year through April 30th of the
current year; that in May of this year, 2,827 notices were prepared and mailed to all
property owners with a delinquent balance as of April 30, 2023; that the delinquent
amounts totaled $421,850; that since the notices went out, some delinquent accounts
have been paid and payments will continue to be received until July 31st; and that staff
recommends that the Board forward the delinquent properties to City Council with a
recommendation that the delinquent properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless
the outstanding balance is paid by July 31st.

Further, Ms. Garcia indicated that at last year’s public hearing, Board Member Garcia
requested an update on how much of the outstanding amount was received by the City;
that the outstanding amount totaled $159,612.39; that the amount recovered was
$152,389.17; that $135,633.39 was payable to Athens Services and the City retained
$16,755.78.

EMERGENCY BOARD-UP COSTS
Report on the cost of emergency board-ups and the hearing of any objections of
property owners liable to be assessed for such abatement in accordance with the
provisions of Chapter 15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Code Compliance Inspector
Cortez presented a report stating that this is an annual report on the emergency board-
ups for the work performed during the year 2021/22; that, as required, the property owner
was provided notice that unpaid invoices are processed as a special assessment to the
property; and that a “Declaration of Substandard” was filed with the Los Angeles County
Recorder’s Office; that on March 21, 2022 a warrant was issued for 15700 Pioneer
Boulevard; that the City has been unable to contact the property owner; that Norwalk
Municipal Code Section 15.32.150A allows the City to board up an unsafe structure; that
the total amount due to the City is $1,932.18; and that staff recommends that the listed
property be forwarded to the City Council with a recommendation that the delinquent
amount be placed as a lien on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance is paid
prior to August 1, 2023.

Chair Apodaca closed the public hearing as there were no persons wishing to testify.

As none of the Board members had any questions or comments, it was moved by Board
Member Barragan and seconded by Chair Apodaca to direct staff to forward the listed
property to the City Council with a recommendation that the delinquent amount be placed
as a lien on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance is paid prior to August 1,
2023.

AUTHORITY

Norwalk Municipal Code Section 8.48.280, Mandatory Service, requires all solid waste
collected from a residential or commercial/industrial premise for a fee, service charge, or
other consideration, shall be collected by a solid waste enterprise under the provisions of
an exclusive contract awarded by the City Council.
INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

City procedures state that any owner who has a delinquent account as of May 1, 2024 which
covers the period of May 1, 2023 to April 30, 2024 shall be sent, by mail, written notification
that the Appeals Board will review all such delinquent accounts during a public hearing. On
May 1, 2024, Athens Services, the City’s solid waste hauler, mailed 2,493 notices that
sought a combined amount of $436,068. As of June 6, 2024, there are 1,138 accounts that
have not paid off their balance.

AUTHORITY

Section 15.32.150.E of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the Building
Rehabilitation Appeals Board to hold hearings related to work completed on private
properties to eliminate a hazard or to remove an unsafe condition or take any action that
would result in a cost assessment against the property.

Section 15.32.150.A of the NMC declares buildings public nuisances, if they are found
“structurally unsafe or not provided with adequate egress, or which constitute a fire
hazard, or are otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use
constitute a hazard to safety or health or public welfare, by reason of inadequate
maintenance, dilapidation, obsolescence, fire hazard, disaster damage, or abandonment,
as specified in this Code or in any other effective ordinance or statute.” Further, such
buildings shall be abated by repair, rehabilitation, improvement, removal, or demolition,
in whole or part, in accordance with the procedures specified in the NMC.

Section 15.32.170 of the NMC authorizes the Building Official to serve as the record
owner and person having control of buildings that are deemed unsafe and pose a safety
hazard to the adjacent community and accords the Building Official authority to prevent
unauthorized persons from gaining access to such structures.

Section 15.32.170.12 of the NMC establishes emergency procedures for the Building
Official to remedy immediate hazards to unsafe buildings or structures by limiting access
to such buildings or structures by order of Sheriff, Public Safety Director, or the Chief of
the Fire Department after giving such notice to the record owner or person in charge or
both as circumstances permit or without any notice if immediate action is necessary.

BACKGROUND:

Staff takes emergency action to secure or otherwise abate the hazardous conditions to
protect the public whenever unsafe conditions are found to create a hazard to safety,
health or public welfare, by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, fire hazard,
disaster damage, vandalism or abandonment.

When the City steps into secure properties and incurs a cost, the property owner on
record is sent an invoice for such work. Unpaid invoices are processed as a special
assessment to the property. Further, a “Declaration of Substandard” is filed with the Los
Angeles County Recorder’s Office as part of the nuisance abatement process to notify
interested parties of the pending cost associated with the abatement.

The purpose of the meeting tonight is to provide the opportunity for any interested party
to voice their concerns or objections to such assessments before the Board.

DISCUSSION:

Notice of the abatement expenses are sent as an invoice to the property owners of record.
Staff keeps an account of the abatement expenses and maintains the list of unpaid
invoices as an itemized written report to the Property Maintenance and Building
Rehabilitation Appeals Board for confirmation (Attachment No. 1). Property owners liable
to assessment may bring objections of such assessments before the Board.

The Board shall hear all objections or protests of property owners liable to be assessed
for the delinquent fees and may make revisions to the report and recommendations to the
City Council with regard to disposition of the delinquent fees.

Upon the recommendation of the Board and confirmation by the City Council, the cost of
abatement will constitute a lien on the property and may be paid to the Director of Finance
prior to August 1, 2024. The unpaid liens will be delivered to the County Auditor to be
collected at the time and in the manner of other taxes on the property.

Attachment No. 1 details the properties that were invoiced for emergency board-up
performed pursuant to Chapter 15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code for which
reimbursement has not been received.
